candidate.blueprint_locator: Printed p.12, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — review medication interactions and adverse effects and evaluate appropriateness of medication orders
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — tramadol and SSRI serotonergic interaction
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize serotonin syndrome as a serious serotonergic interaction risk when tramadol is combined with an SSRI.

options.A: Severe hypokalemia from additive renal potassium wasting.
options.B: Prevention of serotonin toxicity because tramadol blocks central serotonin receptors.
options.C: Serotonin syndrome, because tramadol can contribute serotonergic activity and concomitant serotonergic drugs such as SSRIs increase this risk.
options.D: Loss of opioid analgesia because SSRIs universally prevent tramadol from acting at opioid receptors.

candidate.rationale: Current tramadol labeling warns that serotonin syndrome can be life-threatening and has occurred with tramadol, particularly during concomitant use of serotonergic drugs; SSRIs are specifically listed among those drugs. C is therefore correct. A is not the documented interaction, B reverses the serotonergic risk, and D overstates an interaction that is neither universal nor the serotonergic toxicity asked about. Tramadol also has a separate seizure warning, so the stem was narrowed specifically to the serotonergic interaction to avoid a competing safety construct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Tramadol can cause potentially life-threatening serotonin syndrome, particularly with concomitant serotonergic drugs including SSRIs.
candidate.source_document_title: Tramadol Hydrochloride tablets, for oral use — full prescribing information

candidate.stem: A client taking an SSRI is prescribed tramadol. Which serious medication interaction is associated with their combined serotonergic effects?
